name: Vegeta
what_it_is: Vegeta is a constant-rate HTTP load testing tool and Go library that issues requests at a user-specified rate per second, explicitly avoiding coordinated omission. It outputs binary result streams that can be piped into its own report, encode, and plot sub-commands.
components: attack — sends HTTP requests at a fixed or infinite rate and writes binary result stream to stdout or a file
report — reads result stream and outputs text summary, JSON metrics, histogram, or HDR histogram plot data
encode — converts result stream between gob (binary), JSON, and CSV encodings
plot — generates an interactive HTML latency-over-time chart from result stream
Go library (github.com/tsenart/vegeta/v12/lib) — embeds the attacker, metrics, and targeter types for programmatic use
built-in Prometheus exporter — optional HTTP endpoint (prometheus-addr flag) exposing request_bytes_in, request_bytes_out, request_seconds, request_fail_count metrics during an active attack
protocols: HTTPS with mutual TLS (client cert + key flags)
Unix domain sockets (unix-socket flag overrides host address)
measurement: Requests: total count, sustained rate, throughput (successful only)
Bytes in / out: total and mean per request
HDR histogram output compatible with hdrhistogram.github.io plotter
Prometheus metrics: request_bytes_in, request_bytes_out, request_seconds (histogram), request_fail_count
configuration: -rate: requests per time unit, e.g. 50/1s or 0/infinity for max speed (default 50/1s)
-duration: how long to run the attack; 0 = run forever (default 0)
-workers / -max-workers: initial and maximum goroutine count (default 10 / unlimited)
-connections: max idle connections per target host (default 10000)
-max-connections: hard cap on connections per host
-timeout: per-request timeout, 0 = disabled (default 30s)
-targets / -format: target list file in http or json format (default stdin / http)
-header: repeatable flag to inject request headers for all targets
-body: file whose content is the default request body
-output: result file path (default stdout)
-http2 / -h2c: toggle HTTP/2 with or without TLS
-insecure: skip TLS certificate validation
-keepalive: reuse TCP connections (default true)
-redirects: max redirect hops, -1 = do not follow but count as success (default 10)
-dns-ttl: DNS cache TTL, -1 = disable, 0 = cache forever (default 0)
-resolvers: comma-separated custom DNS server addresses (non-Windows only)
-root-certs: trusted CA certificate files (comma-separated)
-session-tickets: enable TLS session resumption
-max-body: cap on response body bytes captured, -1 = no limit (default -1)
-lazy: stream targets lazily to reduce memory at cost of per-hit latency
-name: label attached to all results for identification in reports
-prometheus-addr: address for Prometheus scrape endpoint (empty = disabled)
-connect-to: static host:port override mapping (round-robins duplicates)
-unix-socket: route all connections through a Unix socket
-laddr: local IP address to bind (default 0.0.0.0)
-cpus: number of CPUs to use (default = system CPU count)
-profile: enable cpu or heap profiling
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection; vegeta is a load generator, not a chaos tool
Can target deliberately slow or error-returning endpoints to simulate degraded upstream behaviour
Configurable redirect handling (-redirects -1) to treat redirects as successes without following
Custom DNS resolvers allow redirecting traffic to different hosts without code changes
modes: Constant-rate mode: -rate N/s sends exactly N requests per second regardless of response time
Infinite-rate mode: -rate 0 combined with -max-workers models N concurrent users sending as fast as possible
Finite duration: -duration stops the attack after the specified wall time
Infinite duration: -duration 0 runs until the process is killed
Streaming targets: -lazy reads targets one at a time to support unlimited or dynamically generated target lists
Distributed mode: run one vegeta instance per machine at rate/N, collect .bin files, report on aggregated files
Library mode: embed vegeta attacker in Go code for custom orchestration
constraints: No docker-compose file in the repository; the Dockerfile builds a single static binary image with ENTRYPOINT vegeta — all sub-commands must be chained via shell pipes outside the container
Rate upper bound is machine-dependent; file descriptor and process ulimits must be raised manually (ulimit -n, ulimit -u) before high-rate attacks
Prometheus scrape timestamps are server-side, not result-time, so latency samples are imprecise; no pushgateway or remote-write support yet (tracked in issue #637)
Setting -rate 0 with very high -max-workers can exhaust resources and crash the process
The Prometheus exporter endpoint is only live during an active attack and closes immediately when the attack finishes, making tail-end scrapes unreliable
docker_services: Single-stage final image: alpine:3.18.0 with /bin/vegeta binary (built from golang:1.20-alpine3.18)
No docker-compose; no auxiliary services (database, proxy, sidecar) are defined in the repository
notable_absences: No built-in scenario scripting or request sequencing (unlike k6 or Gatling)
No GUI or web dashboard — HTML plot is the only visual output
No assertion/threshold enforcement — pass/fail logic must be implemented externally by parsing JSON report
No cookie jar or session management
No gRPC or WebSocket support — HTTP only
No built-in distributed coordination — distributed runs require external SSH orchestration (e.g. pdsh)
